name: windsor-castle
documented_evidence: RCT identifies Upper, Middle and Lower Wards, Round Tower, State Apartments and St George Chapel. Mapped chapel rectangle is72.4×38.7m including transepts, center(-160.4,-48.6)m in the local8-degree frame; its long axis has local heading69.1deg. Named Horseshoe Cloister geometry defines its bent open ranges. Royal Household2016–17 report documents lead roof renewal in the Upper Ward; RCT restoration account confirms St George’s Hall roof reconstruction.
modeling_qualifications: Production anchor62.7m includes the motte. Upper Ward terrain sample52.4m establishes model base; the9m motte reaches61.4m, while Lower Ward offset−8.7m gives43.7m near the chapel. These are production terrain controls, not an independent geodetic survey. Roof/tower heights and bay counts are architectural estimates. Source perimeter grades follow surveyed terrain and ownership follows individual mapped buildings/walls. Upper Ward roof fields are separately pitched behind parapets, with gray lead88 and hall slate86. Chimney placement, roof slopes and different tall hall/three-level residential bay rhythms are scaled architectural estimates; these are not a roof survey.
attribution: Original procedural metric mesh; no downloaded mesh or photo textures. Map ring evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), via Protomaps. Operator texts/images are referenced, not redistributed.
review_status: All3LODs validated and actual-engine capture visually reviewed on frozen app ca938100f84a3acc203e177603e20398a5d4e760e7c7ef4ff915a5de59a0673c. No obvious buried base or source-building interpenetration in reviewed view. Finer architectural dimensions remain estimates where qualified above.
